rules: Shared chain beads have one physical ID and multiple ring memberships; loop indexing does not duplicate objects.
Source m=15 mechanical and m=8 CT chains remain different preparation families unless an actual documented remanufacturing link is supplied.
Three cycles, four cone averages, nine/twelve SMA cycles, 11/31 layers and pictured configurations never establish independent sample counts.
Thread replacement creates a new thread ID and assembly version; a physically distinct network creates a new sample ID.
Glue, knots, crimps and clamp remounts are preparation/state events; irreversible changes cannot be erased by reset.
Replacing a failed component or specimen keeps the failed predecessor and replacement linkage.
A raw record cannot be reused under another sample/material/tension label.
Mechanical-to-CT overlap is null until confirmed by actual custody and identity records.
A sample has exactly one physical location; service custody does not duplicate it.
Required-part preparation binds input-stock IDs, physical output IDs and their current locations; supplied outputs preserve the same identities.
Robot weaving consumes actual prepared bead IDs at their recorded location; preparation never teleports stock back to storage.
WS_ANALYSIS is a data/service handoff only and cannot update specimen location or custody.
